item.title: Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor | Colonial Heritage Hotel Siem Reap
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor is the most historically significant hotel in Cambodia. Opened in 1932 — the same year that international access to the Angkor temple complex was properly established — the white French colonial building on Siem Reap's central boulevard has stood witness to nine decades of the country's history, hosting kings, archaeologists, film stars, and diplomats in its 119 rooms and suites.

The hotel's meticulous heritage restoration preserves the grand original lobby, its carved Khmer columns, dark teak floors, and the celebrated Elephant Bar — the oldest functioning bar in Cambodia, still serving the Singapore Sling recipe that has been unchanged since 1932. Butler service is standard across all room categories, and the dedicated concierge team coordinates private dawn temple access, river excursions, and golf programmes at both Angkor Golf Resort and Phokeethra Country Club.

For AGS groups that value context as much as comfort — where the story of the destination is as important as the quality of the bed — the Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor is incomparable. No other property in Cambodia delivers this depth of authentic heritage narrative alongside a genuine five-star service standard. When the conversation returns to "where did you stay in Siem Reap," the answer "Raffles" requires no further explanation.

AGS coordinates Raffles d'Angkor stays with Angkor Golf Resort and Phokeethra Country Club packages.

item.title: Amanpuri Phuket | The Original Aman Resort Thailand

item.content:encoded:
Amanpuri is not a hotel. It is the original template against which every luxury resort that followed has been measured. Opened in 1988 on a private Phuket peninsula, Ed Tuttle's low-rise Thai pavilion design — rising amidst 30 acres of coconut palms above Pansea Beach — established the radical proposition that true luxury is defined by what is absent: crowds, noise, and compromise.

The 40 pavilions and 34 villas that cascade down to the Andaman Sea each command a private outdoor terrace designed as a second living room — day beds, outdoor dining, and panoramic sea views framed by traditional Thai architectural detailing. The spa, set within a restored traditional Thai temple, offers holistic treatments that have attracted the world's most private and powerful individuals since opening day.

For AGS clients who have simply had enough of settling for less, Amanpuri makes the case that no golf course is more important than where you wake up before playing it. Blue Canyon Country Club, Phuket's finest test, is 20 minutes away. The property's private fleet of longtail boats and speedboats ensure island excursions between rounds are executed with the same effortless precision as everything else here.

Amanpuri is exclusively accessible via direct request. AGS coordinates all reservations and Phuket golf programmes.

item.content:encoded:
Park Hyatt Saigon stands at the intersection of history and ultra-modern luxury in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. Facing the iconic Opera House on Lam Son Square, the hotel's white colonial facade belies an interior of sleek Vietnamese design — dark teak floors, lacquered artwork, and a rooftop pool that frames the District 1 skyline in a way that feels distinctly cinematic.

For golfers, the Park Hyatt's positioning is strategically unmatched. Tan Son Nhat Golf Course — a Nelson & Haworth 36-hole complex — is literally five minutes from the hotel entrance. Long Thanh Golf Resort, Royal Long An, and Taekwang Jeongsan are all reachable within 45 minutes, providing access to southern Vietnam's most diverse collection of parkland and waterside courses from a single, convenient urban base.

The AGS concierge team uses Park Hyatt Saigon as the standard anchor property when designing southern Vietnam golf itineraries for international groups. The combination of location, service culture, and dining quality — headlined by the award-winning Opera restaurant — consistently exceeds the expectations of even the most well-travelled golfers.

item.content:encoded:
Black Mountain Golf Club in Hua Hin is, quite simply, the benchmark for Thailand golf — and for many international ranking panels, the benchmark for Asian golf. Carved directly from a granite mountain on the outskirts of Hua Hin, the course offers visual drama and strategic depth in equal measure, with the natural rock formations, canyon-style valleys, and sweeping ridge views making every hole a genuine event.

At 7,375 yards from the back tees, Black Mountain is a genuine championship examination. The exposed granite boulders serve as both aesthetic masterstrokes and penalty-zone hazards, and the greens — fast, firm, and beautifully conditioned year-round — demand proper reading of the full hole before committing to an approach.

AGS considers Black Mountain essential on any Thailand golf itinerary. It is the course that consistently generates the most enthusiastic feedback from returning discerning clients — the combination of extraordinary visual setting, perfect conditioning, and genuine challenge is unmatched in the region.

item.content:encoded:
Cascata Golf Club takes a refreshingly playful approach to course design in a Bangkok market that can sometimes takes itself too seriously — delivering 36 holes of inventive, entertaining golf that manages to be genuinely challenging while also being undeniably fun. The hallmark features are the unusually large, multi-tiered greens and the creative bunkering arrangements that require golfers to think laterally about approach shots and putting.

Water plays a persistent strategic role across both layouts, with fountains, lakes, and streams appearing in locations that demand respect without being unnecessarily punishing. The overall tone is of a course designed to generate excellent memories and good scoring challenges rather than to intimidate or frustrate — a genuine strength for group golf.

AGS recommends Cascata for Bangkok programs that include mixed ability groups, corporate golf events, or societies looking for a Bangkok round that prioritises shared enjoyment over pure championship challenge. The 36-hole capacity also makes it excellent for full-day group programs without course congestion.

item.title: Chi Linh Golf | Northern Vietnam's Most Challenging Course
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Chi Linh Golf is uniformly regarded as the hardest course in Northern Vietnam — a title it wears with pride. Carved through a dramatic pine-forested valley in Hai Duong Province, the layout's significant elevation changes, narrow corridors, and true bentgrass greens combine to create an unrelenting challenge.

Earning the nickname "the Dalat of the North" for its cool mountain air and rugged terrain, the course winds through ravines and along ridgelines with little room for error off the tee. The fast, true bentgrass surfaces — rare in Northern Vietnam — demand precision on every approach.

For the serious discerning golfer who wants to put their game to the ultimate test, Chi Linh Golf is the benchmark. AGS regularly programmes it on challenge-focused itineraries for groups seeking a genuine step up from the standard Hanoi resort circuits.
